Meet Your BCC · Day 2 of 7 — The four things you own.

When agents ask me what "owning your AI Operating System" actually means, this is what I show them. Four layers, all yours:

YOUR AI (Claude) — reasons, reads your persistent memory, uses your tools, talks to you.

YOUR DATABASE (Supabase) — 80+ tables holding every financial event, staff record, and rule you've taught the system. You can query it. Back it up. Migrate it. Extend it. Yours.

YOUR WEBAPP — the interface your team clicks through every day. Modify a module. Add a module. Ask your Claude to build a new one for a specific workflow your agency runs. Yours.

YOUR INTEGRATIONS — Gmail, Drive, Calendar, GitHub, QuickBooks, Facebook, LinkedIn. Connected to your accounts, working on your behalf.

Compare this to SaaS: someone else's database holding your data, someone else's UI that changes when they decide, someone else's integrations rate-limited by their pricing tier. When you cancel, you lose access to everything.

Your BCC works the opposite way. You own the layers. Your Claude builds and maintains them. Your business shapes the system, not the reverse. And there's nothing to cancel — because there's nothing being rented.

Tomorrow: Following a dollar. What happens between SF's commission email and your dashboard tile — all inside a system you own.

captions.linkedin:
Meet Your BCC · Day 3 of 7 — Following a dollar.

One thing separates a real Operating System from a dashboard: it moves your data without waiting to be asked. Here's what happens between the moment SF pays you a commission and the moment your dashboard reflects it — no manual step at any point, entirely inside a system you own.

① 6:00 AM CDT — Your Compensation Statements come in.
② 10:00 AM CDT — Your workflow reads them via Gmail, parses each product line, and writes to your commission-recap table.
③ 11:00 AM CDT — Your GL Writer scans for unposted rows. Writes cash-basis journal entries to your ledger: cash up, commission income up.
④ Immediately — your income-statement view is a live union of your journal and your QuickBooks mirror. Every P&L, YTD, and margin calc reflects the new number instantly.
⑤ 12:00 UTC — Your Producer Underperformance watcher checks each producer's month-to-date pace against their rolling average. Anyone below 70% gets an alert queued for tomorrow's dashboard.
⑥ 7:00 AM CDT next day — Your daily briefing lands in your inbox with the summary.

What you did: nothing. You woke up. Your system did the plumbing.

Every step above happened inside YOUR database, using YOUR workflows, connected to YOUR accounts. Not a vendor's server. Not a shared platform. Yours.

Meet Your BCC · Day 4 of 7 — Twelve workflows your Claude built for you.

Here's the difference between a SaaS product's automations and workflows inside a system you own: theirs are pre-baked features the vendor decides to build. Yours are workflows your Claude built specifically for your business — and will extend, tune, or replace anytime you ask.

The twelve running today:

Daily rhythm — your daily briefing email (7 AM CDT), email archiver (8 AM), Compensation Statement reader (10 AM), GL writer (11 AM), social publisher and monthly close monitor (9 AM), producer underperformance watcher (12 UTC).

Every six hours — your bank statement reader, credit card reader, deduction statement reader, payroll notification reader.

Monthly — your Producer Production Report parses on the 1st and feeds your Performance tab, commission detail, AIPP pace projections, and producer ROI model.

Every workflow lives in one table in YOUR database. Each writes its result to a log so you can see what happened. If one fails, an alert queues on tomorrow's dashboard — your system tells you, you don't have to check.

Need a thirteenth workflow? Ask your Claude to build it. Need to change how one runs? Ask your Claude to change it. Need one paused during a season? Same conversation.

You don't file a support ticket with a vendor. You talk to your Claude. And your Claude builds on YOUR system.

Meet Your BCC · Day 5 of 7 — The piece most people miss

When you tell your Claude "I pay my producers on the SMVC rate of 10.00% for P&C — remember this" — that fact doesn't live inside "your" Claude.

It gets written to YOUR persistent memory table, in YOUR database. Every future Claude conversation reads YOUR table at the start.

Lose your laptop. Start a fresh chat next Tuesday. Open your BCC on your phone.

Your Claude will still know your SMVC rate, your CPA's name, your producer roster, and the tone you prefer to be spoken to in. Because the knowledge lives in YOUR database — not in the Claude model, not on a vendor's server.

You're not training a Claude. You're teaching your database. That's what makes it get smarter every week. And that's why it's yours.

captions.linkedin:
Meet Your BCC · Day 5 of 7 — You're not training a Claude. You're teaching your database.

This is the piece most people take longest to internalize, and it's the whole thesis of the product.

When you tell your Claude "I pay my producers on the SMVC rate of 10.00% for P&C — remember this" — that fact does not live inside the Claude model. It gets written to a table called persistent_memory in YOUR Supabase database. Every future Claude conversation reads that table at the start.

The knowledge follows YOUR database, not the model.

That's why you can lose your laptop, open your BCC on your phone tomorrow, or start a fresh chat with a different device six months from now — and your Claude will still know your SMVC rate, your blended rate, your AIPP goal, your producer roster, your CPA's name, the SF rules that shape every response (AIPP requires 60 months of service), and the tone you prefer to be spoken to in.

This is also the deepest proof of ownership. In a SaaS product, that intelligence lives on the vendor's servers under the vendor's control. If you cancel, you lose it. In your BCC, that intelligence lives in YOUR database, on YOUR infrastructure, under YOUR control. If Anthropic releases a new model tomorrow, your memory persists into the next conversation. If you want to migrate, back up, or extend it — you can.

Every conversation you have with your Claude makes the next one sharper. Six months in, you'll notice you're never re-explaining your business. And you own that compounded intelligence — not rent it.

captions.linkedin:
Meet Your BCC · Day 6 of 7 — Yours to keep. Yours to grow.

Your BCC ships in three tiers. The reason isn't packaging — it's that a solo agent and a 5-producer team-scaled agency need different starting points. Whichever you pick, you own what you get from day one, and your Claude keeps building on it from there.

BASE ($2,999, one-time) — the operating foundation. 16 modules covering money, sales, people, content, operations, and reference. Enough to run a single-desk agency well. Yours.

PREMIUM ($3,999, one-time) — Base plus a team operations suite: PTO, time tracking, sales activity, handbook, benefits, personnel files, licenses, leads tracking, and the AI coaching module. 28 modules total. Yours.

SUPERDUPER ($5,999, one-time) — Premium plus the producer-factory layer: policy pipeline with per-producer aging, side-by-side producer performance, scorecards and configurable dashboards, per-producer compensation modeling, pay-period close automation, recoup queue for chargebacks, and multi-office roll-ups. 36 modules total. Yours.

All three tiers: one-time setup, zero recurring fees, 30 days of hands-on support after handoff. Base builds in 8–10 business days. Premium in 12–15. SuperDuper in 15–20.

And after handoff, your Claude keeps building on whatever tier you started with. A new workflow, a new module, a new view your CPA needs — you ask your Claude. Because you own the system. There's no vendor roadmap to wait on. Your business shapes it, not the other way around.

Same foundation. Same Claude. Same database. Yours to keep, yours to grow.
